findings.title: PyYAML: incomplete fix for CVE-2020-1747
findings.description: A vulnerability was discovered in the PyYAML library in versions before 5.4, where it is susceptible to arbitrary code execution when it processes untrusted YAML files through the full_load method or with the FullLoader loader. Applications that use the library to process untrusted input may be vulnerable to this flaw. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system by abusing the python/object/new constructor. This flaw is due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2020-1747.
findings.one_line: Admin-uploaded YAML reaches the vulnerable PyYAML FullLoader in the worker.
findings.reasoning: The worker decodes tenant configuration from a queue job and passes it directly to yaml.FullLoader in PyYAML 5.3.1. That version's FullLoader can execute code when untrusted YAML abuses the python/object/new constructor. The 256 KiB limit does not restrict YAML constructors. The upload path is described as an internal admin-console feature, so the supported attack surface is someone able to submit or influence those bundles, not an arbitrary public user.
findings.vulnerable_path: Admin-console YAML upload → tenant_config queue job config_b64 → load_tenant_config(raw) → yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.FullLoader) → python/object/new constructor.
findings.attack_surface: A workspace admin, or anyone able to influence a workspace admin's uploaded YAML bundle, can trigger parsing in the worker.

evidence.quote:
Workspace admins upload YAML config bundles through the internal admin
console whenever a tenant changes integration settings; the worker
parses them as part of the tenant_config job.

findings.recommended_action: Upgrade PyYAML to at least 5.4 and replace FullLoader with a safe loader; test the admin console's custom merge tags before deployment.
findings.patch_hint: Use yaml.safe_load(raw.decode("utf-8")) after replacing the custom !!merge representation or adding only its required safe constructor to a SafeLoader subclass.
